versions.short: The resolution would express the sense of the House that United States policy should diversify its supply of critical minerals so that foreign entities of concern cannot restrict or raise the cost of American access, and would encourage closer, mutually beneficial partnerships with African countries that produce these minerals. It would urge increased investment in African mineral production and processing, financing and technical help for American and friendly African businesses, and turning an existing electric vehicle battery agreement among the United States, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Zambia into a wider investment program. It would also urge the Secretary of State and other federal agencies to develop a five-year strategy covering commercial diplomacy, financing for African producers, equity funds for mining projects, and stronger economic cooperation.
